name: Lance
comments:
40 m was nice and quiet which was fortunate as I heard Mark, VK2KI, calling without his signal making any impact on my S-Meter.  We exchanged our reports, but I was missing too much due to minor QSB to make a more substantial conversation viable.  The circuit must have been solid as he was copying me well, with the contrast put down to output power differences given Mark was once again operating his FT-817.

I then moved up to 20 m to listen for our DX crew.  Unfortunately nothing from Fausto or Willie, but Mike's signal was booming (relatively) into my station S5.  I tried calling but could hear plenty of other stations calling him too, so rather than add to the cacophony bowed out and will try again next week.

I took a break for dinner, and was subsequently called away so unable to return for another session.
caption: Not a skerrick of Mark's signal on the S-Meter during our QSO

comments: 40 m: Sat at home in England, working a radio near Adelaide on the far side of the world, is a bizarre experience. Great fun though. I worked Ian VK5CZ who was QRP but only 150 kms away and coming in strong and clear with lovely Morse. It was great to hear David VK3DBD too, whom I'd previously only heard directly DX from the UK! I tried to work Mark VK2KI but some strange crackly interference got in the way. I then heard Jim VK7JZ working David VK3RU/P on Norfolk Island but, frustratingly, I couldn't raise either of them. But a good morning's work nonetheless.

name: Mark
heard40: VK7TA, VK3KEV,  ZL1BOP, VK5CZ, VK3AAP, VK2VCA, VK2DLF, VK3DRQ
comments:
[15m]
I slid up to 15m at the sked time for Edi DO2EMR at Stuttgart, and even tried calling with my 6W;  not a sausage from Edi this week.

[20m]
Willie DJ9FM was coming through at RSN 311 - Q5 on QSB peaks;  however, not surprisingly, he couldn't hear my 6W - oh well!

[40m]
At the get-go Gerard VK2IO/p was coming through from Wialkutting Nature Reserve so a quick exchange of RSN/RST got me warmed up for the evening;  great to hear a pile of our family giving Gerard numbers for his VKFF park activation.

Next up a CQ led to an RSN 581 call from our Editor Lance VK7TO at Margate.  Lance reported RST 419 and the needle wasn't moving at his end.  Couldn't help myself - quick mental calculation.... 8 S-points difference equates to 48dB, 48dB over my FT-817's 6 Watts looked like his ERP was in the order of 36kW;  pretty good for a TS-520S with a pair of 6146Bs in the final!  I suggested that he might need to re-work his excellent Electromagnetic radiation records that he keeps for his station.

When I signed from Lance, I heard some key-clicks coming through my narrow CW-filter.  A strong station nearby who couldn't hear my QRP I expected.  Then just before calling CQ, something made me slide up the band, and I caught the tail of John VK3BSE's call - 820Hz up the band.  When no-one replied, I took a punt and gave him a call - sure enough he was calling me.  I told him he was 820Hz high (well outside my receiver's passband), and he tentatively dropped by 400Hz - wondering what I was on about.  Subsequent emails confirmed that he'd broken out his signal generator and digital counter to see what was going on with his Icon IC-735.  Seems that the manual doesn't mention any need to offset the receive frequency by 820Hz on CW (unlike most of the older transceivers from the late 70s and earlier) - so the mystery continues!  Have fun with the research mate - perhaps an On My Workbench article to follow?

Next up I heard Clive ZL1CJB in Auckland in QSO;  when he finished I tried... but 6W across the Tasman sea wasn't on the cards this time, which was a pity - been quite a while since I spoke to Clive.

Next up, a huge signal from Ross, VK3/M0NNK transmitting on the new OTAMA remote station belonging to our Ian VK1HF, located just North of Terang in South West Victoria.  Unfortunately, Ross couldn't hear me, but went on to chat to Ian VK5CZ at Clare and David VK3DBD at Yack-and-and-ah (great location for sending your QTH by CW!).  Ross seemed to disappear mid-sentence, so suspecting an internet glitch, I jumped in to say g'day to David while he waited.

After David, I heard James VK7JZ/p out and about again... that's three weeks in a row by my calculations!  James reported that he'd been practicing head-copy while walking to work, which had helped keep his ears in during his recent absence from the airwaves.  Back at the Queen's Domain in Hobart, this time he was keeping and eye on the clock - not wanting to be locked in at 9pm this week.

I finished my transmitting with a quick exchange with David VK9/VK3RU who was over on Norfolk Island;  nice signal to the mainland David.  A bit later I heard Darrin VK3AAP at Sandringham calling David without success;  I also tried calling Darrin but he couldn't hear me.  Had a quick listen on 80m and when I came back to 40m, I listened-in to Greg VK5KFG at Willunga chatting to VK2VCA;  unfortunately, Greg couldn't hear me when I called. 

[80m]
I had a quick listen on 80 and could hear Sava VK4PN calling;  however, I could see some activity on Ian VK1HF's IKARA KiwiSDR at Spring Range near the ACT boarder on 40, and having not changed my antenna coupler's settings, went back there to see what was going on.  By the time I returned to 80m, Sava had gone, and my CQs went through to the aether.

But all-in-all, a really fun night of QRP QRS (and probably other Qs) for me.
caption: John VK3BSE was sent scurrying to the signal generator and frequency counter by my off-frequency report.

name: Sava
comments:
Not much to report for the last Tuesday's QRS Net, managed to join only for 30 minutes at the very end. Called and listened on 80 m for about 20 min no takers and no one heard. I checked my signal into vk6 and could just see it at vk6qs Augusta SDR. At Ironstone SDR it was solid red but boy the waterfall looked awful orange and red with only  few lines of blue indicating terrible QRN and high level of noise. vk1hf SDR looked ok but my carrier was the only trace so I gave up and moved to 40 m for the remaining 10 min. After few CQ QRS calls Mike vk6tx/4 came back and we had a standard QSO exchange. Signals were good both ways as Mike is at Harvey Bay which is a nice skip distance from my QTH. Mike is coming back into CW so we kept at low speed. I wonder if using a paddle and transceiver inbuilt CW keyer makes life more difficult for those just starting or trying to improve CW proficiency due to the lack of control. With straight key operator is in full control of dots and dashes ( length, spacing ) and tempo no need to concentrate on what is poring out of the rig for you as there is enough trouble just concentrating  on spelling and content. In the past I used both electronic keys and  Bugs but these days I use only a straight key. Nothing gives you " On Air "  personality as the straight key.
Tuesday is worst day for me regarding QRS Net as I get only occasional Tuesday when I do not need to pick up my grand kids from school and take them to all those after school activities. By the time everything is finished  ( swimming, gymnastics, music ) I am lucky if I make it home by 10:30 UTC.
